comment: Patch art (issue #133, of #131, design guide 2.0): one embroidered merit-badge-style patch per species per edition, painted by FLUX.3 Image Klein from the species' reference bird isolated on white (<ref_image_0>), lying flat on white card under even, diffuse light so the app does the lighting. FLUX.3 reads a caption of the finished picture. No template names the species: the reference is the identity. `editions` holds each set's patch: its shape, the merrowed cord's colour, the twill ground and the stitched motif, by pack id (the edition's look; its name and theme stay in the pack's set). `dark` is added for a reference bird whose median lightness (L*) is under `dark_lightness`: in the samples thread lightened dark birds and invented pale patterns (a black phoebe, a cedar waxwing), while the same words for every bird blackened a House Finch's blue-grey belly. Kept apart from prompts.json so a patch change never repaints pack art. Version 2 (the maintainer's review of the Los Angeles patches, 2026-11-04): `settings`, one per species from its `art.setting` in the pack's overrides.json, since version 1 put every bird on a branch, ducks and shorebirds included; and {markings}, the plumage facts the maintainer gives for a species the thread keeps getting wrong (`art.patch.markings`), which describe the bird and never name it. A new version does not repaint a patch that was reviewed (the review is the costly part); a rejected patch takes the current templates. Bump the version when a template, a setting, an edition or the clause changes.
template: A product photograph of an embroidered merit badge shaped like {shape}, photographed from directly above, lying flat in the middle of plain white card under soft, even, diffuse light, with only a faint shadow. The badge is {twill} finished with a thick raised merrowed border of overlocked {cord} thread all the way around its edge. On it is embroidered the bird from <ref_image_0>, exactly as it appears there: the same pose and angle, the same feather pattern, colours and markings, the same bill, eye, legs and proportions, and the same sex and age (a dull female or young bird stays dull), nothing added and nothing taken away, rendered entirely in thread.{dark}{markings} Only the bird comes from <ref_image_0>, none of the branches, leaves or background around it. Its feathers are laid in dense long-and-short satin stitches whose direction follows each feather tract, the thread colours matched to the bird's own, and its eye is a tiny glossy black satin dot with one white highlight stitch. {setting} Behind it, inside the badge, a few simple fill-stitched shapes suggest {motif}. Every thread is visible: the soft sheen of rayon, the raised stitches, the woven twill between them. The whole badge is in the frame with a margin of white card all around it, in sharp focus. No text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere. No other birds, animals or people.
dark: Where the bird is black or nearly black in <ref_image_0> it is stitched in black thread, and its white and pale parts in white or pale thread, with the same contrast as the reference.

us-ca-la.motif: a few glossy citrus leaves, and low chaparral hills under a warm golden sky

us-ca-sd.motif: sandstone sea cliffs, a few ribbons of kelp and a soft hazy sky

us-ca-bay.shape: a regular hexagon lying on one flat edge, with a flat edge along the top, a flat edge along the bottom and a point at the left and at the right
us-ca-bay.motif: banks of fog rolling over oak hills and a few tall redwoods

us-ca-desert.shape: an arch, rounded at the top with straight sides and a flat bottom
us-ca-desert.motif: a Joshua tree, a fan palm and a rose-gold dusk sky

us-fl-orlando.shape: a shield, rounded at the top and coming to a soft point at the bottom
us-fl-orlando.motif: cypress trees, saw palmetto fronds and a misty lagoon

us-pnw.shape: a five-sided pentagon standing on a flat bottom edge, with a single point at the very top
us-pnw.motif: a few tall dark fir trees, a snow-capped mountain and drifting grey mist

us-ny-nyc.shape: a square with generously rounded corners
us-ny-nyc.motif: a skyline of tall city skyscrapers rising close behind the leafy treetops of a city park, with a strip of park lawn below

us-la-south.shape: a diamond, a square stood on one corner, with softly rounded points
us-la-south.motif: tall bald cypress trees with flared trunks standing in dark swamp water, long grey-green curtains of Spanish moss draped from their branches

settings.perch: Its feet grip a small embroidered branch that runs across the badge beneath it; it does not float.
settings.trunk: It clings upright to the furrowed bark of an embroidered tree trunk that fills one side of the badge, its feet and stiff tail braced against the bark. There is no branch under it.
settings.ground: It stands on the ground, stitched as a low band of earth with a few blades of grass and pebbles around its feet. There is no branch.
settings.rock: It stands on a low stitched rock only a little longer than the bird. There is no branch.
settings.shore: It stands on wet sand at the water's edge, stitched as a low band of pale sand with a few ripples and shells around its feet. There is no branch.
settings.wade: It wades in shallow water stitched in bands of blue thread, its legs in the water, with a few reeds beside it. There is no branch.
settings.water: It swims on calm water stitched in horizontal bands of blue satin thread across the lower part of the badge, sitting low in the water with no legs or feet showing, small ripples and its reflection around it. There is no branch and no perch.
settings.flight: It flies across the badge with its wings as in <ref_image_0>, just above a small embroidered branch.
